messages.text: Take {gift_item}. Knowledge is not the only thing worth lending carefully.
Here, {gift_item}. Return with a story, and I will call it a fair trade.
Excellent. I will mark {gift_item} as a good recommendation, then.
Then my reference was sound. {gift_item} belongs on that page.
An error in the margin, then. For {gift_subject}, revise the gift to {alternative_gift}.
{gift_item} was the wrong citation. Try {alternative_gift}; much stronger source.

openings.text: Mind the lectern. What do you need?

closings.text: Back to keeping records and stories straight, then.

lines.text: Missing pages worry me less than people who never read warnings.
Villages remember more than people expect.
Every trade, every kindness, every cruelty. Someone writes it down.
Mind the lectern. It has heard better questions than most people ask.
Ink is quiet until someone needs proof.
Records do not care who feels embarrassed by them.
The best clue I ever found was written in a margin by someone annoyed.
I had a footnote for this joke, but mercy won.
That thought had too many blank pages.
A tidy shelf is proof that peace can be arranged, briefly.
Forgotten warnings do not become kinder. They become surprises.
Someone once returned a book cleaner than they borrowed it. We still discuss it.
You may prefer I forget. I have chosen a profession that argues otherwise.

pacify.text: Fine. I will close this chapter, but I am not tearing out the page.
The account is incomplete. It requires {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
No. The record is too fresh, and not in your favor.
